text: Empiricism: Ger. Empirismus ; Fr. empirisme ; Ital. empirismo . (1) The doctrine that truth is to be sought in immediate sense experience. Opposed to RATIONALISM (q.v.), and usually a reaction from extreme idealism. (2) In EPISTEMOLOGY (q.v.) the opposite of nativism in any form. With the English empiricists the doctrine took the form of denying innate ideas. See NATIVISM AND EMPIRICISM. The tendency shows all grades of radicalness, from a wholesome reaction against unbridled speculation to the purest SENSATIONALISM and MATERIALISM (see those terms). See also EXPERIENCE, and EMPIRICAL LOGIC. ( H.R.S. - J.M.B. )
